In a small town called Pipitown, there lived a girl named Lily. Lily was a bright and talented young
girl, but she often found herself unhappy with her life. She yearned for more excitement and adventure,
wishing she could escape her everyday routines. Lily attended a local school where she excelled in her
studies and had a few close friends. However, Lily often felt like something was missing. She spent
hours daydreaming about faraway places and envying the lives of others she saw on social media.
One day, during a school assignment about gratitude, Lily's teacher asked the class to write about
what they appreciated most in their lives. While her classmates wrote heartfelt essays about their
families, friends, and simple joys, Lily sat at her desk feeling sad and empty. As she glanced around the
room, she saw her peers immersed in their writing, their faces reflecting genuine warmth and affection
for the people and the experiences they held dear. However, when Lily tried to write something, she
struggled to find anything she truly valued. Despite her academic achievements and supportive family,
each time she tried to write something she was grateful for, nothing came out. She felt frustrated.
As weeks passed, Lily's dissatisfaction with her life grew stronger. She became increasingly critical
of her surroundings and found herself complaining about everything. Her once-bright personality began
to dim, and she withdrew from her friends and family. The only joy she found was when she was able to
browse the internet. She was hooked on following the influencers and admiring their lifestyles. She
began to imagine the life she saw on social media as hers.
One evening, Lily stumbled upon a post about a volunteer programme in another country. The
programme offered an opportunity to travel abroad and work with underprivileged communities. Lily
liked the idea of leaving her town behind and embarking on a new adventure. Without hesitation, Lily
applied for the volunteer programme even though it was not her passion and she was accepted. She
packed her bags and prepared for her journey. She was excited and believed that this experience would
finally bring her the fulfilment she had been searching for.
Upon arriving in the remote village, Lily experienced an eye-opening situation. The living
conditions were basic, and resources were scarce. Yet, the villagers welcomed her with open arms,
grateful for her willingness to help. When Lily was at the village, she witnessed the hardships faced by
the villagers - lack of clean water, limited access to education, and inadequate healthcare. Despite their
struggles, the villagers showed a sense of courage and happiness that left a deep impact on Lily.
One evening, as Lily sat under a starry sky with the villagers, she reflected on her journey. It had
been almost a month since she saw her family. Tears filled her eyes. She thought about how she had
taken her life for granted. After having observed the villagers' lifestyle during her stay, she realised that
true happiness was not found in grand adventures or exotic destinations, but in embracing the present
moment and appreciating the blessings around her.

9 1119/1
When Lily returned home, she was a changed person. She no longer spent a lot of time on social
media. She reconnected with her friends and family, expressing gratitude for their love and support. She
shared her volunteer experience with her classmates, encouraging them to cherish the life they had and
find joy in the little things. She did not have regrets or dissatisfaction in her life anymore.
From that day forward, Lily lived each day with a renewed sense of gratitude and purpose. She
dedicated herself to making a positive impact in her community, volunteering at local charities and
spreading kindness wherever she went. Lily's journey taught her that the greatest adventure is the
journey of self-discovery and that true fulfilment comes from within. She no longer yearned for a life of
excitement of going abroad but embraced the beauty of her own story, one filled with lessons of
gratitude and humility.

Detective Johnson sat at his desk, surrounded by files and photographs. His mind was focused on
the current big case. 27 It was Mrs Thompson, a well-known wealthy woman in the town. She is
famous for her generosity but can be rather annoying at times with her child-like attitude. She came in
looking very anxious and upset. 28 As she sat down, she began to let out a loud cry.
The detective didn't even have to ask what the matter was as Mrs Thompson ranted on and on about
her missing diamond necklace. 29 The detective could not understand what she was saying. He
had to calm her down so that he could make sense of her story. 30 After taking a few sips of the
soothing tea, she was ready to answer the questions that could help solve her problem.
"I attended a charity gala last night. I thought of wearing my diamond necklace but changed my
mind and wore my ruby necklace instead. I'm sure I had locked the drawer properly, but when I woke
up this morning, it was gone," she explained. 31 He examined the scene and interviewed
the staff. He spoke with them at great length. He also discovered a faulty security camera. 32
He narrowed down the suspects to the butler, the gardener, and Mrs Thompson's personal assistant.
They were all assembled at the main living room as instructed by the detective, nervously waiting for the
outcome.

Discovering the World of Flowers
A - ROSES
Renowned for their timeless beauty and captivating fragrance, roses are
iconic flowers with a rich cultural history. They come in a variety of
colours and forms, from delicate tea roses to vibrant blooms, enchanting
gardeners and florists alike. Roses are significant in many parts of the
world. They symbolise love and passion as well as elegance in floral
arrangements.
B - SUNFLOWERS
Sunflowers, large, cheerful blooms with tall stalks, are classic symbols of
sunshine and vitality. These plants are native to the Americas and have
become popular worldwide for their striking appearance and culinary uses.
Sunflowers also provide food and habitat for birds and other wildlife.
These iconic flowers have garnered global admiration for their striking
appearance and versatile uses.
C - ORCHIDS
Orchids are exotic blooms and come in diverse forms and fascinating
shapes across the globe. They can be found in many habitats from tropical
rainforests to moderate climates. Orchids have captivated plant
enthusiasts for centuries with their intricate blooms. In ancient days, Greek
women believed that by eating orchids, they would have baby boys.
D - TULIPS
Tulips boast a spectrum of coloured blooms and they indicate the arrival of
spring. The name tulip is derived from a Persian word for turban. Tulips
flower in the spring and become dormant in the summer. They are
synonymous with Dutch culture and are cherished for their simplicity and
beauty. Tulips have been one of the main attractions to lure tourists
worldwide to visit The Netherlands.

13 1119/1
E - LILIES
Lilies are elegant flowers with their graceful trumpet-shaped petals and
strong fragrance. They bloom in various sizes; colours and they symbolise
purity. There are 111 species in this lily family. The Chinese believe that
harming the lilies may bring damage to the environment. Lilies are also
important in cultural and religious ceremonies around the world. White
lilies are popular at weddings and funerals too.
F - DAFFODILS
Daffodils are generally white and yellow and has six petals in its distinct
trumpet-shaped corona. Daffodils symbolise new beginnings. There are
about 36 species of daffodils around the world. Each of these flower types
brings unique beauty and significance to the world of gardening, floristry,
and natural landscapes, enriching our lives with their colours, scents, and
cultural meanings. It became an important commercial crop in
The Netherlands by the 19th century.
